extracted.intended_audience: broadcast journalists, news producers, and journalism students
extracted.subtask_description: Selecting and producing radio and television news stories using Boyd's broadcast-focused news values, selection filters, and production-quality markers. Emphasizes what makes a story suitable for broadcast formats and how to craft it for radio or TV.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proximity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A story's nearness to the audience increases its newsworthiness; local or culturally close events matter more to viewers/listeners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure of practical impact on audience lives — policies, services, safety, economy — determining whether the audience cares because it affects them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediacy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that are current or unfolding have higher value for broadcast; immediacy is especially important for radio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that tap into audience curiosity or unusualness attract attention even if not high-impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drama
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of conflict or a clear narrative arc increases engagement; drama helps sustain attention in short broadcast formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entertainment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that entertain — human-interest, quirky, visually or sonically appealing — can be appropriate for broadcast alongside harder news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radio — Strength is immediacy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Radio must constantly update; quick turnaround and real-time reporting are core strengths to exploit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radio — Voice quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviewable subjects with good voice quality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjects should sound well on air — clear, expressive voices that carry emotion and clarity for listeners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radio — Sound potential
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should offer usable ambient sound or audio elements that enrich the narrative for listeners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radio — Brevity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Radio copy should be concise and efficient; packaging a story for typical radio time slots requires tight writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radio — Pronounceable names/places
rubrics_metrics.description: Names and places should be pronounceable on air
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid tricky names or prepare clear pronunciations; clarity matters for listener comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radio — Active voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Use active voice for drive-time clarity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer active constructions to maintain energy and clarity, particularly during peak listening periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Television — Visual potential
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A TV story should offer compelling visuals; if it cannot be seen, it loses suitability for television.

rubrics_metrics.name: Television — Action over static
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action-packed scenes or movement are preferred to static shots; dynamic visuals keep viewers engaged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Television — Identifiable people
rubrics_metrics.description: People on camera should be identifiable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Viewers should be able to see and recognize subjects; identifiable faces increase connection and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Television — Bites
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short, quotable soundbites (bites) are valuable for TV packages and promos; seek concise, expressive comments on camera.

rubrics_metrics.name: Television — Live capability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that can be covered live add immediacy and value for TV newscasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Television — Graphics-friendly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data and information that can be turned into graphics or on-screen visuals increase a story's TV suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Television — Tease-worthy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that can be promoted with a short tease help drive ratings and viewer retention between segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Can we get there?
rubrics_metrics.description: Logistical feasibility of reaching the story site
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess travel time, access, and whether the crew can physically get to the scene in time to gather usable material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Can we get an interview?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether people are available and willing to be interviewed; interviews are central to broadcast storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Can we shoot/record it?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the necessary recording conditions and permissions exist to gather broadcast-quality sound or images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Can we tell it in 30s-2min?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the story can be packaged into a short bulletin or a slightly longer segment without losing coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Will viewers/listeners stay tuned?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the story will hold attention through its slot and help maintain overall program flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does it fit the 'rundown rhythm'?
rubrics_metrics.description: Fit with the show's pacing and sequencing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate if the story complements the order and tone of other pieces in the newscast/rundown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity and technical quality of audio
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadcast stories require clean, well-recorded sound; poor audio undermines credibility and listener comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity and technical quality of video/images
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sharp, well-framed, and properly exposed imagery is necessary for professional television presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anchor delivery
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchors should deliver copy clearly, naturally, and with appropriate tone to suit the story and audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporter on-scene
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of a reporter at the location
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On-scene reporting lends authority and immediacy; being there enhances credibility and provides original material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fresh material (vs. file footage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Newly gathered material rather than archival
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original, recently recorded material is preferable to reused file footage to keep stories current and engaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple voices in story
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of different speakers/points of view
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Featuring more than one voice (experts, witnesses, authorities) adds balance and richness to the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original reporting visible
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of the reporter's own reporting work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should show original reporting (interviews, on-the-ground observations) rather than purely repackaged information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story can be heard/seen
rubrics_metrics.description: Story must be suitable for audio (radio) or visual (TV) presentation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that are only readable without audiovisual elements are less suitable; ensure sensory elements exist for the medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: People available for interview
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability of spokespeople, witnesses, or affected individuals is a key determinant of a story's viability for broadcast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visuals exist (TV) / Sound exists (radio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Existence of usable visuals or sounds
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm that TV stories have visual elements and radio stories have compelling sound to tell the story effectively in the medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief enough for format
rubrics_metrics.description: Concise enough to fit program constraints
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should be compressible to the time slots available without losing essential meaning or impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatic enough to retain attention
rubrics_metrics.description: Has drama to keep audience engaged
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should include elements of tension or human interest that sustain attention across the segment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live moment when possible
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finding or creating a live element increases immediacy and viewer interest where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotable for tease
rubrics_metrics.description: Capability to be teased/promoted during the show
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that can be promoted in short teases help build audience retention between segments.
